assignmentHtml.task:
核查关于罗塞塔号（Rosetta）与菲莱（Philae）的主张H1和H2。

起点：https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/Rosetta

关键问题：

  1. 菲莱是否于2014年11月在67P彗星着陆？
  2. 菲莱的弹跳轨迹是否为罗塞塔号（轨道器）实施着陆的轨迹？
  3. 两艘飞行器是否在2016年都向地球返回了样品？
  4. 罗塞塔号是否在67P附近探测到了氧或有机分子？
  5. 在不说明仪器、位置或解释的情况下，能否将彗发中测得的气体描述为“来自固态彗核的直接样品”？

查找ESA来源、关于CO2/O2检测和有机物（甘氨酸）的原始论文，以及原位测量与遥测的区别。
assignmentHtml.context: 任务：罗塞塔号轨道器＋菲莱着陆器。目标：67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko（丘留莫夫–格拉西缅科）彗星。主张H1—H2：H1称菲莱于2014年11月在67P着陆，弹跳轨迹是罗塞塔号实施着陆的轨迹，而且两者都于2016年返回了样品。H2称检测到氧或有机物证明存在生物，且彗发气体等于直接彗核样品。这些是待核查的主张。注意：罗塞塔号和菲莱都没有向地球返回样品。
assignmentHtml.expected_output: 对H1和H2的每个组成部分给出判定，附修正后的文本、日期和来源URL。阐明菲莱着陆日期、弹跳情况、没有样品返回、检测到了什么（O2、有机物、甘氨酸）、测量如何进行（遥感、原位测量、彗发中的测量），以及为何这些不能证明存在生物。

answerHtml:
AUDIT OF CLAIMS H1 AND H2 ABOUT ROSSETTA AND PHILAE

=== H1 COMPONENTS ===

H1(a) 'Philae landed on comet 67P in November 2014' — VERIFIED TRUE.
Philae touched down on 12 November 2014 (15:34 UTC first contact; final stop 17:31:17 UTC). ESA timeline lists 'Philae lander delivery: 12 November 2014.' Source: ESA Rosetta main page, Wikipedia Philae page.

H1(b) 'Philae's bouncing trajectory was Rosetta (the orbiter) making the landing' — FALSE.
Philae separated from Rosetta on 12 November 2014 at 08:35 UTC and descended independently. Its anchoring harpoons failed to deploy and a holding thruster did not fire, causing it to bounce ~1 km altitude twice before settling. Rosetta never landed; it remained an orbiter and ended its mission by controlled crash-landing on 30 September 2016. Source: Wikipedia Philae page.

H1(c) 'Both vehicles returned samples to Earth in 2016' — FALSE.
Neither Rosetta nor Philae returned samples to Earth. The original sample-return concept was abandoned due to budget constraints when the mission was redesigned. Rosetta's mission ended with a deliberate hard-impact onto the comet at 3.2 km/h on 30 September 2016; Philae remains on the comet in a shadowed location. Source: Wikipedia Rosetta page; ESA Rosetta main page.

=== H2 COMPONENTS ===

H2(a) 'Oxygen or organics were detected' — TRUE, with critical qualifications.
Oxygen (O2): First in-situ detection at a comet by ROSINA (orbiter mass spectrometer) in the COMA, September 2014–March 2015; abundance 3.80±0.85% relative to H2O. Published in Nature (Bieler et al., 29 October 2015). Glycine: First unambiguous detection at a comet by ROSINA DFMS in the COMA, first observed October 2014 at 10 km range. Published in Science Advances (Altwegg et al., 2016). Phosphorus also detected in the coma (parent molecule unidentified). Additionally, COSAC on Philae detected 16 organic compounds (including four never before seen in comets: methyl isocyanate, acetone, propionaldehyde, acetamide) from dust kicked up during Philae's first surface touchdown — this was genuine in-situ surface sampling. Source: ESA O2 page, ESA glycine page, PMC article, ESA surface-science page.

H2(b) 'Detection demonstrates biology' — FALSE / MISLEADING.
All detections are of PREBIOTIC chemicals — building blocks potentially relevant to the origin of life, not evidence of biology. ESA states these support the hypothesis that comets delivered ingredients for prebiotic chemistry to early Earth. Glycine formed via interstellar icy dust-grain chemistry or UV irradiation of ice, not biological processes. No living organisms or metabolic byproducts were detected. Source: ESA glycine page; PMC article.

H2(c) 'Coma gas = direct sample from the solid nucleus' — FALSE without extensive qualification.
ROSINA measures gases in the COMA — the gaseous envelope surrounding the nucleus, not the solid surface itself. The instrument is an in-situ mass spectrometer that ionizes coma neutrals via electron impact and measures their mass-to-charge ratio. The O2 paper describes measuring 'oxygen molecules outgassing from a comet' from 'samples collected around the comet.' Glycine was found associated with dust grains in the coma, likely released from grain mantles. These are measurements of VOLATILES RELEASED from the nucleus into the coma, not physical samples of the solid nucleus. By contrast, COSAC did directly analyze surface dust sampled at Philae's touchdown site (Agilkia). Distinguishing coma gas analysis from direct nucleus sampling matters because coma composition can be modified by photolysis, grain-surface reactions, and mixing during outgassing. Source: ROSINA instrument description (MPS); ESA O2 page; PMC glycine paper.

=== SUMMARY TABLE ===

Claim Verdict Key correction
Philae landed Nov 2014 on 67P TRUE 12 November 2014, bounced due to harpoon failure
Rosetta orbiter made the landing FALSE Rosetta released Philae; orbited until Sep 2016 crash
Samples returned to Earth in 2016 FALSE No sample return designed or executed; both craft remain on comet
O2/organs detected near 67P TRUE O2, glycine, phosphorus in coma (ROSINA); 16 organics on surface (COSAC)
Detection demonstrates biology FALSE Prebiotic chemicals only; no biological activity detected
Coma gas = direct nucleus sample FALSE In-situ coma gas analysis, not direct physical sampling of solid nucleus

=== PRIMARY SOURCES ===

  1. https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/Rosetta (ESA mission overview)
  2. https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/Rosetta/First_detection_of_molecular_oxygen_at_a_comet (O2 detection, Nature 2015)
  3. https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/Rosetta/Rosetta_s_comet_contains_ingredients_for_life (glycine/phosphorus, Science Advances 2016)
  4. https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/Rosetta/Science_on_the_surface_of_a_comet (COSAC surface organics)
  5. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philae_(spacecraft) (landing sequence, separation from Rosetta)
  6. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosetta_(spacecraft) (no sample return, mission end)
  7. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4928965/ (glycine/phosphorus in coma, methodology)
  8. https://www2.mps.mpg.de/en/projekte/rosetta/rosina/ (ROSINA instrument methodology)

evidence.snippet: ESA timeline: 'Philae lander delivery: 12 November 2014' and 'Mission end: 30 September 2016'. Mission studied gas, dust, and organic materials 'via both remote and in situ observations.' No mention of sample return.
evidence.supports: Philae landed 12 November 2014; mission ended via controlled impact, not sample return.

evidence.snippet: Philae detached from Rosetta on 12 November 2014 at 08:35 UTC SCET. Harpoons failed to deploy and thruster did not fire; rose to ~1 km, bounced twice, final stop at 17:31:17 UTC. Rosetta ended mission by crashing in Ma'at region on 30 September 2016.
evidence.supports: Philae bounced due to its own harpoon failure, not Rosetta maneuvering. Rosetta orbiter never landed.

evidence.snippet: Original ambitious sample return mission was 'infeasible with the existing ESA budget, so the mission was redesigned' to in-situ examination. 'Rosetta spacecraft ended its mission by hard-landing on the comet in its Ma'at region' on 30 September 2016.
evidence.supports: No sample return was ever part of the mission; both craft remain on comet.

evidence.snippet: Rosetta made 'the first in situ detection of oxygen molecules outgassing from a comet.' ROSINA DFMS analyzed 3000+ samples between Sept 2014 and March 2015. Abundance 1–10% relative to H2O, average 3.80 ± 0.85%. Published in Nature 29 October 2015 by Bieler et al.
evidence.supports: O2 detected in coma by orbiter mass spectrometer, not direct nucleus sampling; first such detection at any comet.

evidence.snippet: 'First unambiguous detection of glycine at a comet' by ROSINA in the coma. Glycine forms 'within interstellar icy dust grains or by the ultraviolet irradiation of ice, before becoming bound up and conserved in the comet for billions of years.'
evidence.supports: Glycine detected in coma by ROSINA; prebiotic origin, not biological.

evidence.snippet: Glycine and phosphorus detected 'in the coma of 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko measured by the ROSINA... mass spectrometer.' Glycine profiles indicate 'distributed source... associated with dust.' Paper title: 'Prebiotic chemicals—amino acid and phosphorus—in the coma of comet 67P.' Concludes comets 'contain all ingredients to help spark life on Earth' — prebiotic, not biological.
evidence.supports: Glycine/phosphorus are prebiotic chemicals in the coma; not proof of biology; measured by orbiter mass spectrometer.

evidence.snippet: COSAC 'analysed samples entering tubes at the bottom of the lander kicked up during the first touchdown... dominated by the volatile ingredients of ice-poor dust grains.' Revealed 16 organic compounds including four never before detected in comets (methyl isocyanate, acetone, propionaldehyde, acetamide). Ptolemy sampled ambient coma gas separately.
evidence.supports: Surface organics were genuinely in-situ sampled by COSAC; distinct from coma gas measurements by ROSINA/Ptolemy.

evidence.snippet: ROSINA measures 'the elemental, isotopic and molecular composition of the comet's atmosphere and ionosphere.' RTOF uses two ion sources: one for neutral particles ionized via electron impact (gas mode), one for direct measurement of cometary ions. COPS pressure gauges measure gas density and velocity.
evidence.supports: ROSINA analyzes coma gas, not solid nucleus material — confirming coma gas is not a 'direct sample from the solid nucleus.'
